req.title: DELETE is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on second and subsequent DELETE calls for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states DELETE /players/{squadNumber} must be idempotent: first call returns 2xx (204), second call returns 404. The endpoint uses squad_number as the path key. Tests cover: (1) positive - first DELETE returns 204, (2) state transition - second DELETE returns 404, (3) boundary - DELETE on squad_number=1 (lowest in DB) then repeat, (4) negative - DELETE on non-existent squad_number returns 404 immediately, (5) decision table - verifying exact status codes on both calls to catch operator/constant mutations.

tests.name: test_delete_get_confirms_resource_gone_after_delete
preconditions: Player with squad_number=12 exists in the database
trace: R-PLAYER-030: state transition - resource transitions from exists(200) to deleted(404) and stays deleted
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_get_confirms_resource_gone_after_delete():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r_get1 = client.get('/players/squadnumber/12')
    assert r_get1.status_code == 200
    r_del1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/12')
    assert r_del1.status_code == 204
    r_get2 = client.get('/players/squadnumber/12')
    assert r_get2.status_code == 404
    r_del2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/12')
    assert r_del2.status_code == 404

test_delete_get_confirms_resource_gone_after_delete()
